Emily —

Great questions. I pulled in Vivek (our Head of Security) to provide precise technical answers; see his notes below. High level answers first, then Vivek's details.

High level: 
- Support access is always session-based and auditable. Engineers do NOT have standing access to customer data.
- We enforce a privileged access workflow: access is granted through a time-limited privileged access ticket with at least one approver outside the support engineer's direct team.
- All privileged sessions are recorded in the audit log with user, timestamp, justification, and session duration. Logs are stored in the customer's selected region by default; retention is 90 days by default with options for longer-term retention (legal/compliance tiers).
- Customers can request custom roles via the Console. We provide a UI for custom role creation with permission granularity (read, write, admin) across resources.
- Separation of duties: operational roles are separated from audit/export roles; data export actions require an elevated workflow and approval.

Vivek Kulkarni (Head of Security) — added comments: 
"Emily / Tom — quick technical details: 
1) RBAC model: shipped roles include account_admin (full config + billing), dev_ops (deploy/manage models), read_only (view-only), support_agent (session-level troubleshooting). Customers may create custom roles scoped to teams or projects. Custom roles inherit least-privilege defaults.
2) Support access / break-glass: When support access is needed, an engineer opens a Privileged Access Request (PAR) that includes the customer ticket id and justification. The PAR is routed to a designated approver (customer-configurable or Redwood-appointed), and approval requires at least one approver independent of the engineer's on-call rota. Upon approval, a temporary session token is issued that expires after a configurable window (default 2 hours).
3) Logging & immutability: All privileged-session metadata and API actions are logged to an append-only audit store. Audit logs are written to object storage in the customer's chosen region (we support us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1, etc.). Default retention is 90 days; for enterprise customers we support 1/3/7 year retention tiers and log archival to customer-managed S3 buckets or partner SIEMs via secure connectors.
4) Data residency: Customer data (model inputs/outputs and KV caches) can be pinned to region-level deployments. Audit logs follow the same residency policy by default.
5) Exports & separation of duties: Data export operations require an Export Authorization workflow (approval + justification) and generate an export artifact with a signed provenance record. Operator accounts do not have unilateral export capability.
6) Certifications: We can provide redacted SOC 2 Type II report and a redacted network diagram under NDA. Document delivery can be via a secure link (we typically provide time-limited signed URLs).

Happy to schedule a 30-minute session to walk through the PAR flow and show the Console. I can demo creating a PAR and the audit trail in a live session.

— Vivek"
